title: What 6 Different Versions of This Sex Comedy Say About the Countries That Made Them
gist: A24's The Invite, an English-language remake of Spanish film The People Upstairs, is one of six national adaptations (Spain, Switzerland, Italy, South Korea, France, Hollywood) of the same script produced within roughly six years, an unusually fast and organic cross-cultural remake cycle the author uses to compare how each culture localizes the same sex-comedy premise.

themes.theme: An unusually fast, organic multi-country remake cycle

insights.claim: The A24 film The Invite, directed by and starring Olivia Wilde alongside Seth Rogen, Edward Norton, and Penélope Cruz, is a remake of the 2020 Spanish film The People Upstairs (Sentimental) by Cesc Gay, and between 2020 and 2026 four additional versions were produced in Switzerland, Italy, South Korea, and France, with a Belgian/Dutch version also in production.
insights.speaker: Jordan Hoffman
insights.so_what: Six national remakes of one script within six years is a notable and possibly unprecedented cross-border IP replication pattern in film, illustrating rapid, low-cost content localization as a production strategy that other low-budget, single-location IP could replicate.
insights.locator: The People Upstairs came out in 2020

insights.claim: The author argues this remake wave differs from the early 'talking pictures' era practice (e.g., Paramount on Parade's 13 language variants, Universal's Spanish-language Dracula filmed on the same sets as the English version) because it is not a single studio maximizing profit from one production, but an organic, independent recognition across separate national film industries that the story resonates locally.
insights.speaker: Jordan Hoffman
insights.so_what: Signals a shift in how content travels across markets — independent, decentralized adaptation rather than centralized multi-language production — relevant to how streaming-era IP and format licensing might increasingly work.
insights.locator: But there's a key difference between then and now

insights.claim: A practical production driver behind the remake wave is that local film industries, still recovering from COVID-era production constraints, found a one-location, four-performer film cheap and easy to produce.
insights.speaker: Jordan Hoffman
insights.so_what: Highlights low-budget, single-location scripts as a resilient, low-capital content format that national film industries gravitate toward during periods of production cost pressure.

themes.theme: Cultural localization patterns across the six versions

insights.claim: Each national version alters specific plot and character details to reflect local sensibility: the male lead's profession changes (rock musician in the U.S., classical pianist in Spain/Switzerland, jazz musician in Italy, a stalled TV director in South Korea), and the upstairs woman's ethnic-coded 'exotic' dish varies (flan for the Spanish-American Cruz character, unspecified spicy Indian food in Spain/Switzerland/Italy, tapas in France, fried eggplant in South Korea).
insights.speaker: Jordan Hoffman
insights.so_what: A concrete illustration of how identical IP is culturally re-coded market by market — a useful case study for entertainment/media analysts assessing localization strategy beyond simple dubbing or subtitling.

insights.claim: The French version is the outlier in tone and stakes: it adds a twist where the couple's off-screen daughter is actually a 20-year-old seduced by the upstairs neighbor, doubles the orgy-participant number to 20 from the 4-10 used in other versions, and leans toward the marriage ending in breakup, similar to the Hollywood version, while Spain, Switzerland, and Italy suggest reconciliation and South Korea's ending is the most unambiguously positive about the couple's new open arrangement.
insights.speaker: Jordan Hoffman
insights.so_what: Shows how ending-tone divergence (reconciliation vs. breakup vs. transformation) across near-identical scripts can serve as an informal proxy for cultural attitudes toward marriage and sexuality, of interest to media analysts studying content-market fit.
insights.quote: We're supposed to be libertines together!
insights.locator: All six versions of the movie build to their conclusion
